chapters.title: Chapter 1244: Kent’s Debt
paragraphs: As expected, when the Sky Fox learned they would be migrating, they all became thrilled. Finally, their years of torment and torture would come to an end.
They used to live in lavish houses, eat proper food, and enjoy peace of mind when their Priestess was alive. However, after the Sky Priestess died, their life turned upside down.

The humans and Beasts ruled them with an iron fist, depriving them of the peace and tranquillity they once had. Had it not been for Yuyin’s bravery, this partial peace they had for the past 5,000 years wouldn’t have been possible.
Now, however, they are about to move in with their Princess, who left, running for her life from her own father. Of course, in the past, most of them hated the idea of a human being their Princess.
However, when they learned she was the one who killed their oppressors and that the dragon that came with her was the infamous Kent Madson, everyone couldn’t contain their happiness.
They readily started packing their loads to move into their new home.
Meanwhile, Liora and Kent ended their quick kiss when Yuyin returned and took Liora away to meet some of the Sky Fox.
She had been away for a long time after all.
Kent, on the other hand, used the time to enter the tower and chat with Gaia, who had already started overseeing the building of the new city for the Sky Foxes.
Kent knew he had no tower points left to use for the Floating City project. The last time he checked, he owned 1.2 billion in tower points.
Of course, if everything were calculated, what he owned would be less than 500 million tower points. However, after Gaia met Li Hua, she changed and began to love money.
So his debt is now in the billions. But despite his debt, he needs help yet again. The Sky Foxes need a city to stay in, and the only one that can help is Gaia.

When he arrived in the Mountain Garden, the two people he threw there had been locked away in the Tower Prison since Uncle Drew didn’t want the little ones to see the kind of torture Avotha was putting them through.
Gaia and her people are busy at work.
"Big brother, you are here." Seeing Kent appear, Gaia and her minions ran and hugged him. They were happy to see him. In fact, they were always so glad to see him.
Kent also enjoys spending time with them, so he welcomed the hug.
"Yes, I am here. I miss you girls," Kent replied, brushing their little heads. After the hug, Gaia looked at him and smiled.
"I assumed big brother is here to negotiate his debt."
Kent smiled but nodded. This made Gaia grin and manifest an eyeglass. Seeing this, Kent knew he was in trouble.
"Follow me, big brother. The plan is ready, and as usual, it is going to cost you." Kent shook his head, and with a forced smile, he followed her.
Uncle Drew and the demigods could only smile as they watched a legendary figure like Kent get dragged around by a midget whose love for money was insatiable.
When they reached the area where the building plan was, Gaia waved her hand, and a 6-foot scroll opened for Kent to see the plan.

Although he is not an architect, he was able to read the plan. It is a large city located on a floating island. The buildings will be made from jade stones but will also feature modern, even futuristic aesthetics.
Most of the buildings will be floating in the air since the Sky Foxes like to fly around. The ground buildings will also be made to fly into the air if the owner wants to.
In short, the city they had in mind will be magical. However, Kent knew such a design would come at a steep cost, so he was both happy and unhappy at the same time.
Gaia intentionally chose this design so she could swindle him out of money.
Of course, a long time ago, Kent promised her he would let her build the tower into something they both would like. So far, she had done a fantastic job.
But the cost is just too much to handle.
"I assume this is worth a fortune," Kent said, and Gaia smiled, adjusting her glasses. Behind her, the Lolis smiled, making Kent wonder just what kind of debt he would be stepping into now.

"I always strive to give Big Brother the best. So, since this is the time to build the tower city into a magical place, I ought to use the best materials. This, of course, is why the master will need 2 billion tower points for this project.
Of course, since the master is broke, I am willing to give him a loan that expires in 5 months (outside time).
After five months, if the master doesn’t pay 70% of what he owes me, I would be forced to trigger the Gaia Quest, where the master will be forced to work nonstop to pay all he owes me."
Kent furrowed his brow, hearing her threatening words. "Are you threatening me?"
"Of course not. I am merely telling Big Brother the consequences of taking advantage of cosmic beings."
Somewhere at the core of the universe, Lady Universe laughed, feeling amused. Since Gaia is a cosmic being, no harm would come to the universe if she were to make the heart of the universe laugh.
She is also a cosmic being, so no karma is involved.
Kent narrowed his eyes at Gaia, who smiled and extended her small yet cute hands. "Do we have a deal, Big Brother?" She used her other hand to adjust her glasses.
Kent, of course, had no choice but to accept her deal. "You have yourself a deal, Gaia. But if I find out you had scammed me again, then you’d better prepare to be spanked till you cry blood."
Gaia pouted and pulled out her little tongue. She had secured yet another contract to build yet another magical city.
Once she is done, what Kent owes her will amount to 3.2 billion.
Of course, Kent knew the tower points, while useless to him and his wives, cosmic beings have a use for them. So he would work hard to pay his debt.
But getting 3.2 billion tower points now will require a lot of slaughter. ’I’d better get on it fast,’ Kent turned and walked away.

Since the location of the planet Kaelith has not been communicated to Uncle Drew yet, Kent instead went to the Legion Tower to get his legion ready for another expedition into the Planet Killer dungeon.
Every last person inside the tower adds to the tower points whenever they kill, so he knew, for now, they would have to farm tower points for him.
When they saw him enter the Legion Tower, they all became happy.
"Master, are we going on a mission?" Kaizo asked, already jacked and ready for some battle.
"Yes. However, you have to give the ladies 12 more days to be ready. The 5th floor is going to be hard, so you all should prepare well before venturing there."
They nodded, already happy to be back on a mission.
Kent stayed for a few hours checking up on all his legion. Once he was satisfied, he left and went back to Tianxu, where the Sky Foxes were still preparing to migrate.

chapters.title: Chapter 1245: Aala
paragraphs: At best, it would take Gaia 8 days to build the city. She already has a plan, so the next best thing is to start building.
But since that was just 8 hours on the outside, Kent decided to spend them there. Once they are done migrating, he will head to Planet Bayla, which is much closer to the edge of this galaxy.
Words had already spread throughout the floating island city that the ones who had come to their rescue were Liora, their Princess, who many thought was dead, and her husband, Kent Madson.
Yuyin sold the narrative maybe too well, making sure that all who saw Liora as human and thus never wanted her to be their Princess and future Queen would change their minds.
Nobody would be stupid enough to look down on the wife of the legendary Kent Madson. It just isn’t something anybody would dare do.
So when Kent returned to the island, and Liora wasn’t back with her aunt yet, he decided to take a walk.
He is already famous, so he would not face any resistance or scrutiny.
When he walked out of the hall, he was greeted by a little fox girl who was sneaking a peek into the hall, probably trying to see the person everyone was talking about.
"Oh, who do we have here?" Kent said, nearly scaring the living hell out of the little lady. She tried to run, but she calmed down, knowing she had come there to see him.
Many wanted to come, but they weren’t brave enough.
She turned to Kent and spoke, keeping her focus on him as if trying to commit his appearance to memory.
"My name is Aala."
"Oh, such a beautiful name." The name is indeed beautiful for a Foxkin.
But even if it isn’t beautiful, Kent, of course, had already found a liking for the little fox.
He didn’t know if she was also a loli, but considering she is 13 and so small, it wouldn’t be unexpected if her growth buds failed to give her height.
Perhaps because he has over seven of them inside the tower, Kent found Aala likeable.
"Is big brother called Kent Madson?" Aala asked, a little hesitant.
Kent smiled and crouched down. The way Aala was looking at him, if he didn’t reduce his height, she would probably break her neck.
"Yes. I am Kent Madson. Nice meeting you," Kent extended his hand for a shake. Aala looked at his large hand for a few seconds before extending her tiny one.
"Well, Aala, the one who brought me here has abandoned me, so I need a guide. You don’t mind giving this big brother a tour, would you?"
"Aala has lived here for a long time, so of course, Aala will show big brother around."
"Wonderful," Kent lifted her off the ground, causing a yelp to escape her lips. However, when he set her on his shoulder, Aala giggled, feeling very tall.
"Wow, Aala is taller than big brother."
Kent smiled, feeling amused.
"Of course you are. You are a big girl after all."
"Aala is a big girl," she smiled, feeling happy. This made Kent also feel good.
Maybe because he had spent more time around lolis, whenever he is around one, he feels happy. They are just too innocent, both in the way they sound and the way they look.
"So, where to first?"
"Aala will take big brother to the training ground. Aala always goes there to wait for Mother and Father to return from their missions."
"Okay then. Let’s go."
Kent soon left the entrance of the hall and started walking in the direction Aala pointed.
Soon, they were spotted by the Sky Foxes, who were busy packing their stuff. Many of them seemed surprised to see Kent Madson casually walking among them.
Some even seemed shocked to see Aala seated on his shoulder, her little legs wrapped around his neck and her slender yet tiny hands holding his horns.
In their minds, such a legendary person shouldn’t be this down-to-earth.
However, watching Kent converse with Aala, with a handsome smile on his face, they could only let the moment print on their minds.
Kent didn’t mind their looks. He was happy hearing Aala speak in the third person. In a way, his lolis—almost all of them—speak in the third person. They refer to themselves in the third person.
So Aala sounded just like them.
Soon, they were near the arena, where sounds of metal could be heard coming from inside.
Since the Sky Fox only specialises in illusion, their combat power is relatively weak. As a result, once their illusions are broken, they become defenceless.
So to counter that, Yuyin made it a must to train a few of the Sky Foxes in hand-to-hand combat. At heart and in their job class, they are illusionists.
However, when it comes to preserving their lives, knowing a thing or two about handling themselves with weapons is essential.
They called this group of Sky Foxes "Combat Foxes."
Aala’s parents are Combat Foxes, and, from what she told Kent, they are powerful Combat Foxes who venture off the island to search for food for their people.
She always comes to the training arena to wait for them whenever they go on said missions. So she brought Kent to wait for them while they observed the Sky Foxes train.
According to Aala, her parents said they would return today.
When they got close to the arena, Kent flew into the air and landed on the tall wall surrounding the arena. It was open at the top, so when they landed, he could see everything.
Many also noticed him, and as expected, shocked expressions appeared on their faces.
"Don’t mind us. We are just here to observe and wait for Aala’s parents." They nodded and went back to training. Most of them were using the bow, while the rest were training with the sword.
Initial observation already told Kent that they weren’t really good with any of the weapons they were using.
’It is quite pitiful how limitations on one’s bloodline can cause them to live knowing they can never rise above their weaknesses.’
[That is life, Master. Not everyone gets to have it all.]
Kent sighed in his heart.
"Big Brother, aren’t they awesome? Aala wants to be like them when Aala grows her second tail," Aala said with a happy smile, causing Kent to force out a small smile.
"Of course, they are awesome. And I can’t wait to see you swinging your sword when you join them."
Aala smiled, tightening her hold on Kent’s dragon horns. As a Foxkin, once she grows her second tail, she can start cultivating.
It is the same as humans having to wait until they were 16, sometimes 15, before they could start their cultivation journey.
However, seeing that she was already happy to join the Combat Foxes made Kent smile weakly. They aren’t strong enough to his standards; however, to someone like Aala, they are gods.
Suddenly, a portal opened not far from the training arena, and three people came out.
Turning to the portal, Kent saw Liora and Yuyin carrying a lady with a bloody look toward the training arena. He jumped down from the wall and rushed to them.
"Mama," Aala suddenly exclaimed, jumping down from Kent’s shoulder.

chapters.title: Chapter 1246: Planet Modu
paragraphs: Kent wanted to hold Aala back, but in the end, he let her rush to the fox lady whose life was hanging by a thread.
"Mama," Aala took hold of the woman’s hands as tears began to pour from her eyes.

The woman is her mother, whom she had been waiting for. She and her husband left two weeks ago to look for food outside Planet Tianxu for their race, only to return alone, gravely injured and life barely hanging on by a thread.
She is part of the team that mostly goes out through a teleportation gate they found deep underwater. The gate leads to a planet of unintelligent beasts.
So, although dangerous, they always manage to bring home food.
This time, however, only she returned, but not in good shape.
"Big brother, please save my Mama," she turned to Kent, tears rolling down her face as she pleaded for her mother to be saved.
Kent didn’t even have to be told twice. He summoned Elaine, who thankfully had managed to ascend to the Heavenly Ascension stage and came out of seclusion a day ago.
"Kindly save her mother," Kent said with a calm expression, but seeing Aala cry seemed to be affecting him mentally.
Elain waved her hand, and a green energy suddenly enveloped Aala’s mother as if she were scanning her. A few seconds later, her brow raised.

"How barbaric, five of her meridians have been severed, and a curse has been placed on her bloodline. If I attempt healing her, she would die." Elaine paused and then thought for a moment, "The least I can do is keep her alive until the curse is broken."
Kent grit his teeth and quickly asked the tower for a solution.
[The master has two options. First, you can concoct the Purifying Pill using any flame with the purification property. Or second, find the one who cast the curse and kill them.

Although the second option won’t break the curse, it also won’t prevent Lady Elaine from healing her meridians. If the one who cast the curse still lives, attempting to cure her will prompt them to trigger the curse, which will kill her.
So it is either you give her a Purifying Pill or kill the curse caster. The curse can be broken later.]
Kent turned to Yuying... "Where did they go?"

Yuying promptly answered, "Since we are under strict supervision from the humans and beasts, we have to travel outside this planet through a gate hidden underwater. The gate leads to a lawless planet called Modu.
The beings there are unintelligent; however, they have three intelligent rulers called Monarchs. We are on good terms with the Demon Monarch.
It has no planet suppression since it is a lawless world. However, it has food and resources that have been sustaining us for the past 5000 years."

Yuying pointed at Aala’s mother and said, "She is part of a five-warrior team that goes to collect food from the Demon Monarch. They left 14 days ago and were supposed to return today. However, we found her like this when we went to welcome them, as I always do."
Kent nodded and turned to Elaine, "Take her and Aala to your parents and keep her alive. I will tell you when to start healing her meridians."
Elaine nodded and vanished with the mother-daughter duo.
"Liora, go to the tower shop and get the herbs for the Purifying Pill. I will be back soon."
Liora wanted to go with him, but she knew handling the mission Kent had given her was important, too. "You can go with her, Yuyin. I will take it from here."
Kent activated the Soul Map and directed it underwater. It took just a second for him to locate the teleportation gate.
He teleported and appeared in front of it.
"Tower, activate it." The gate activated the next second, allowing Kent to walk through in a heartbeat.
[Planet Modu]
The planet that Kent appeared on looks dull and filled with demonic qi and other energies.
There is not much light in the air, and as much as he would love to wonder just why or waste time reading what his Heavenly Jade Eyes have for him, Kent didn’t come for that.
The entire atmosphere is corrupted, making it dangerous to live there as an intelligent being.
ROAR
He let out a terrifying dragon roar, causing all beasts on the planet to shudder. The entire planet heard the roar, prompting them to look toward its source.
"I know you all can hear me, so listen carefully. You have just a minute to come here now, or else I will slaughter every last beast on this planet. I have no time to mess around."
Kent’s voice spread across the planet, causing even more panic among the beasts and demons living there.
Three seconds later, space cracked and three beings walked out, each radiating the power of a Death Stage beast. That is three realms above the Heavenly Ascension stage.
Although there aren’t many lawless worlds in a High World, such planets have no suppression. They are primarily found in the Immortal and God worlds.
Of course, they are different from Unique worlds and forsaken worlds.
While there is no suppression on such worlds, the beings that live on them can only reach the Death Stage rank if in a High world and True Immortals if in an immortal world.
They can’t leave the planet, and even if someone carries them away, they would never be able to rise above the Death Stage rank.
However, it is said there is a beast contract that can allow the beast tamer to help them rise above the Death Stage.
Kent eyed the three beings, each radiating different auras...

One is a 6-meter humanoid behemoth. It has eight backwards-curved horns etched with abyssal runes. Four muscular arms dripping with black ichor. Wings made of condensed abyssal energy. Eyes that glow with a blood-red hue, and skin made of obsidian-black metal with shifting cracks radiating demonic qi.

The second is a tall, elegant, slender woman with long blue hair flowing behind her like smoke. Although she is no human, she has beautiful eyes that seem to mimic the nebula. Her skin is pale and smooth like polished moonstone. She has elegant, devilish horns, thin and curved to show her deadliness. Kent senses void energy coming off her.

And for the last, he is a towering 8-foot-tall man with a metallic body. He is clad in armour made of fused bones—blue abyssal flames in his eye sockets. A red soul-core exposed in his chest radiates intense abyssal spiritual energy. Behind him float countless corpse puppets.
Kent didn’t sense any threat from them, but he spoke in a commanding tone.
"Someone placed a curse on a lady who was just here and may have killed or taken away her companions. I want that person, and I will be on my way."
Kent extended his hand, and Gaap materialised as a black jagged sword radiating cold mist... "Refuse to comply, and I will kill everybody on this planet."
BOOM
A terrifying aura erupted around Kent’s body, causing the three Monarchs of Modu to shield themselves using their corrupted energy.

chapters.title: Chapter 1247: The Three Monarchs (1) [Xmas Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent didn’t tap into his bloodline, blood runes, or flame veins.
He merely commanded, but his voice reacted with the spiritual energy in the air, causing a powerful pressure to descend on the planet.
He learned that from Chaos.

The three Monarchs, despite being Death Stage beasts, felt their lives threatened. However, instead of acting on the threat and answering the question, Kent asked, they released their aura, cancelling the pressure.
Clearly, they had no intention of complying.

Khar’mol raised a bone scythe, abyssal energy oozing out from it. He pointed it at Kent and spoke in a creepy tone... "You can’t come here and demand answers like you own the place. This is our domain; you have no right here."

He released a wave of energy from his body, causing the corpses standing behind him to react. The red core on his chest emitted a wave of crimson energy, and lines of red energy moved and entered the thousands of corpses standing behind him.
Their eyes turned red, and a powerful aura burst from them, threatening to level the place. They fixed their gaze on Kent, ready to attack when the order was given to them.
The metallic skin on his armour emitted crimson flashes, forcing a metallic pressure on Kent.
Kent felt a wave of metallic qi emanating from him.
This caused Kent to raise his brow... slightly intrigued, mildly amused.
"This is Planet Modu. You have no authority here, so you will do well to respect that," the slender lady, Lilixen, also spoke in a commanding yet beastial tone before releasing a wave of void energy.

It caused the void to tremble, then burst open, releasing thousands of dark swords, each aimed at Kent. A dangerous will is channelled through the swords, causing the ground to tremble under Kent’s feet.
Every last sword will be a threat to a Heavenly Ascension Stage cultivator. However, Kent merely stood calmly, his expression unreadable.
As for the third Monarch, Azrakul, he raised his hand, and somewhere on the planet, a large pillar rose from the ground and started emitting demonic qi from it.
It surged forward, appearing behind him in a flash.
"We were told you would come. However, they said nothing about how arrogant you are." His body expanded, rising to 12 feet tall.
"Now, since you have come, then you might as well stay."
All three had no intention of complying, a clear sign to Kent that someone else was at play. These beasts may lack intelligence compared to real spirit beasts, but they aren’t stupid.

If anything, they are aware of what was about happen, yet they refused to comply with Kent’s request. Of course, maybe they are too high and mighty to listen to his command, or perhaps they don’t want to behave.
But they can sense the danger surrounding Kent, and so they know going against him is a bad idea. However, they still choose to oppose him.
Kent sighs, slightly disappointed.
He expected them to heed his command, but since they refused, he might as well go ahead using the hard way.
"Such a pity. I came with hope to converse with beasts with brains. However, it turned out you three are brain-dead duds." Kent raised his sword, and a wave of sword aura burst out from it.
"This is also good. I can just kill you and read your memories. Then I will beat it out of the person behind it all."
RUMBLE

A thousand blood runes were activated at the same time, causing a dangerous feeling to descend on the planet. Kent channelled his energy through his sword and released a powerful sword aura unfused with blood qi.
"Not on my watch," Lilixen clapped her hands together, and the void trembled, the thousands of swords squeaking.
Behind Kent, a thousand blood runes manifested, hovering in the air. On his arm, dark golden dragon scales moved and coated the sword (Gaap).
The squeaking of the thousand void swords sharpened into a chilling resonance. The void literally cracked, and void qi poured out. The swords absorbed them like hungry lions.
Then all at once, they shot forward like a storm of tearing night. The space trembled, and a wave of energy that could flatten even a Peak Heavenly Ascension Stage warrior erupted from the sword.
Kent didn’t move.
He simply tightened his grip on Gaap.
The black blade hummed, absorbing some of the blood runes floating behind Kent. Kent had already advanced his understanding of blood after experiencing Chaos’ memories.
He mastered the blood runes far beyond merely using them to boost his physical strength. He can now convert them into sword qi.
This gave him the confidence to stand at ease, watching as the swords descended on him with deadly energy.
"What a disappointment."
Suddenly, one command left Kent’s lips, causing the scene to change.
"Cut."
SHRRRINGGG...
A single sword arc flashed, illuminating the sky. However, while it is a beautiful sight, the energy behind it is anything but enjoyable.
If one doesn’t pay attention, they won’t see the arc, since it is as thin as a hair. In an instant, it arrived before the swords.
Every void sword that came close was split in half. Their fragments dissolved into ash-like void particles that scattered across the dark sky without much resistance.
Just that single thin arc was enough to destroy all the void swords with ease.
Lilixen’s eyes widened.
’Impossible...’ she thought, her expression turning pale as she looked at Kent from above.
Kent didn’t even step forward, yet her technique, powerful enough to slaughter thousands of Life Stage cultivators, was destroyed casually.
"You..." she whispered, voice trembling with disbelief.
Kent paid her no attention, since his focus was on the second Monarch, who also made his move.
Azrakul didn’t wait for the heat to die down. He formed a hand seal and muttered coldly.
"Demonic Pillar—Devour!"
The massive pillar he raised earlier suddenly cracked open, releasing tendrils of demonic qi that tore across the sky, whipping toward Kent like starving beasts.
Two blood runes flew and merged with Kent’s fingers. When he channelled his energy into them, they began to emit faint killing intent.
Then, when the tendrils were close enough, he flicked his finger.
BOOM.
The explosion was loud and blinding, a perfect moment for Kent to act.
A burst of wind pressure exploded beneath his feet, channelling the flame veins into his speed.
In an instant, he just vanished. This action caught the Monarchs off guard. However, before Azrakul could register it, Kent appeared over his head, sword raised.
Gaap was already descending in a deadly slash.
Azrakul crossed all four of his arms to block the attack, black demonic qi coating them. He was caught off guard by how fast Kent moved; however, he isn’t exactly weak to begin with.
Even so, Kent gave the classic arrogant remark before his sword connected with his arm...
"Weak"
CLANG!
His obsidian-metal skin cracked under the powerful slash Kent unleashed. However, his nightmare wasn’t over...
A second strike followed.
CLANG!
This time, both arms shattered, spraying black ichor into the air. Kent’s deadly attack shattered the fragile resistance he had mounted.
He was just too fast for any of the three monarchs to match up to him.
Azrakul roared in agony as he was blasted backwards, tumoring through mountains like a meteor. The demonic pillar flickered violently, losing its stability.
Kent raised his head and looked at it, a smirk forming on his lips.
He rotated Gaap once, scattering the blood runes hovering behind him.

Some moved and merged with his sword, raising the sword aura around it and the sword intent in the air. However, before Kent could move to destroy the pillar, Khar’mol, the Bone Monarch, finally acted.
With a screech, he raised his bone scythe and spun it in a deadly arc.
"Corpse Legion—Awaken!" The sky suddenly turned dark.

chapters.title: Chapter 1248: The Three Monarchs (2) [Xmas Bonus]
paragraphs: The abyssal energy in the air surged, moving into the puppets. When it touches them, they release a screeching moan that reacts with the abyssal energy to create a violent shockwave.
’Has some potential. But not enough to face my majestic self,’ Kent thought with a grin.𝑓𝑟𝑒𝘦𝓌𝑒𝑏𝑛𝑜𝘷𝑒𝘭.𝒸𝘰𝑚

Khar’ul didn’t share in his sentiment. With a gesture from his bony hands, thousands of corpse puppets behind him surged forward, red eyes blazing, some sprinting on all fours, others floating, some leaping through the air with sharpened bone claws.
Kent smirked faintly.
’What a comic display of weakness.’ He didn’t want to admit it, but the sight was laughable.
However, inasmuch as he would like to hold his stomach and laugh his brains out, he decided to be the bigger person and let the moment pass.
He came seeking the one who placed the curse on Aala’s mother, but from what he had seen so far, none of the three Monarchs had what it took.
But that also isnt enough to let them off without some beating.
Kent shifted his stance and raised his sword gently. The energy coming from the corpse puppets was perfect for Gaap’s growth.
"Gaap... time to feast."
FWOOOM.
Hearing the command, the ancient demonic sword became happy... ’This is the best. So much resentment.’ Gaap’s voice entered Kent’s mind, making him smile.
Black mist erupted from the sword, condensing into five shadowy jaws that opened beneath Kent and lunged forward like a tidal wave.
Khar’mol instantly sensed danger; however, it was already too late for him to do anything.
The first row of corpse puppets was devoured instantly.
The second row followed.
The third row tried to retreat forcefully, but it was already too late. Kent knew what he wanted from the moment he laid eyes on the corpse puppets. So he made his move when the time was ripe.
Within seconds, thousands were erased, and Gaap kept devouring, even jaw chasing after the ones retreating. They weren’t faster than Gaap, who Kent had reinforced with blood runes.
Khar’mol panicked and slammed the butt of his scythe on the ground.
"STOP!"
Kent grinned and lifted his hand, forcing three blood runes to merge with it... "Why should I? I already gave you a way out, but you didn’t take it. Now, let me kill you in peace."
The merged blood runes on Kent’s hand pulsed, emitting a suffocating killing intent. In an instant, the only energy in the air became a suffocating mixture of blood and sword qi.
Even the demonic winds trembled as Kent’s aura shifted.
It is now chaotic and more chilling than before.

Khar’mol staggered backwards, his face turning even paler. The other two have also distanced themselves from Kent, feeling their lives threatened. It took just one exchange for them to know they were no match for him.
"Stay back!" Khar’mol hissed at his remaining puppets, but Gaap ignored him entirely.
FWOOOOOSH—
The shadow jaws expanded wider, now large enough to swallow a hill. They lunged toward Khar’mol, directly creating a booming echo that kept pushing pressure onto Khar’mol.
The Bone Monarch reacted instinctively.
His scythe spun, carving a crescent slash of abyssal energy that cleaved through the shadows. He poured so much energy into the attack that space trembled when he swung his weapon.
BOOM!
Gaap trembled and recoiled a step, but Kent didn’t.
His flame veins activated, boosting his speed. In the blink of an eye, he appeared above Khar’mol, an evil smile plastered on his face.
Two blood runes moved and merged with his foot.
"This is for disobeying my command." His foot descended, creating a sonic boom.
CRACK! BOOM!
The Bone Monarch’s head was driven into the ground so hard that the land cratered, trembling like an earthquake.
However, as someone who is half-step from becoming an immortal, Khar’mol roared, lifting the scythe despite half his spine cracking. "Abyssal Binding Chains!"
Black tendrils burst from the earth, wrapping around Kent’s limbs and torso. It was his desperate move that yielded no results.
They tightened, abyssal flames burning through them; however, Kent wasn’t fazed.
"Futile."
Kent’s magnificent golden eyes flashed blue, then, as if the Queen of Ice chose to appear on Planet Modu, the entire planet’s temperature plummeted, freezing the land and water.
All over the planet, beasts with low resistance to ice were instantly frozen and then shattered into bits and chunks.
The tendrils binding Kent also turned to ice, and then, with a mere tap of his finger, they shattered, freeing him. However, Kent didn’t stop there.
He extended his hand, and Gaap flew into his firm grip.
"Since this place is a waste, I might as well destroy the planet." The temperature dropped even further, forcing the three Monarchs to activate their domains.
However, Kent just smirked and stomped on the ground...
"Chaos Ice Domain."
A wave of chilling ice washed over the planet, instantly shattering the three domains. It extended further, causing Hundreds of thousands of beasts to die in an instant, but Kent didn’t seem to care.
They aren’t intelligent beasts, after all, so he had nothing to be sorry about. If this were a planet ruled by spirit beasts, he would have considered the innocent casualties.
He raised his sword, and three deadly swords made from blue ice appeared and aimed at the three monarchs"

"Interesting. It seems even without activating the Absolute Ice, I can overpower three Death Stage beasts." A wicked smile appeared on his lips. "I bet using that here will surely render this planet useless after my attack."
"Why don’t I give it a go?"
"PLEASE STOP. WE WILL TELL YOU WHAT YOU WANT TO HEAR!"
Lilixen spoke, her body shivering as if she had taken a bad cold medicine.
"I am not interested, lady. I can just kill you three and extract what I want from your memories."
"PLEASE."
One could see the fear in their eyes.
Initially, Kent just wanted to test how merging his blood runes with his sword aura would work. However, he quickly saw how devastating it could be.
From Chaos’ memories, he saw him merge the blood runes with his claw aura, making every swing of his claw deadly.
However, seeing and actually doing it are two different things. Thankfully, he was able to test it out and knew when he met a worthy opponent, they were going to regret their life choice.
Next, he chose to use his newly acquired ice element to test the three Monarchs. Safe to say, with just 30% of it, the entire planet is about to turn into a ball of ice.
The wind is completely frozen, a testament to how devastating the ice is.
Kent lowered his sword slightly, the three ice-forged blades still hovering behind him like executioners waiting for the command to slaughter.
The frozen winds howled across Modu, and even the ground beneath Kent’s feet crackled under the overwhelming cold.
Lilixen trembled violently, her knees nearly buckling.

Khar’mol’s skull was half-buried in the frost-covered crater, cracks spreading across it like fractured glass. Azrakul, missing two arms, forced himself to stand straight but failed, coughing up black demonic blood.
None of them dared move.
None of them dared breathe too loudly.
Kent’s eyes glowed faintly with icy blue light as the three swords floated closer, shifting their angles to aim at the three Monarchs’ throats.
"One more chance. Just one," Kent said calmly, almost bored. "Speak. Now."
Lilixen dropped to her knees.
"We... didn’t cast the curse," she said quickly, her voice breaking. "It wasn’t us. I swear."
Kent didn’t blink.
He didn’t need to ask for elaboration.
He just waited, knowing they would sing like canaries soon enough.

chapters.title: Chapter 1249: Forsaken Seer
paragraphs: "It was the Forsaken Seer," Lilixen finally revealed, causing Kent to knit his brow. His mind moved on its own, and like flipping through books, the words quickly made sense to him.
Among the many names he was expecting to hear, he most certainly didn’t expect to hear the one name he hated with all his being.
The Forsaken race.
Aside from the Void Beasts, Kent’s most hated enemy is the Forsaken race.

They took something precious from him, and so he promised to kill every last one of them. In the past, he had killed many; however, they are still around, and as such, he would not stop until they are all dead.
With his memories of the Faceless Assassin, he knew even in that life, he had encountered the Forsaken race, and he hated them just like he did during the primordial era.

Surprisingly, the name mentioned just now triggered a memory from that life instead of his life as the Chaos Dragon. This memory was handed to him by a mission he received after he killed the Demon King.
Inside this mission, a Forsaken Seer appeared on a planet that they had marked to be taken over by the Forsaken race.
Since the forsaken race can’t leave their planets, the loophole was to manipulate others to open the forsaken gate in their planets, which will allow them entry to take it over.
However, when this forsaken seer appeared, something strange began to happen.
Many cultivators had started going missing, and from what was gathered, the Forsaken Seer is using them to summon Forsaken beings.

The Forsaken Seer has a peculiar ability that allows them to summon Forsaken beings into the bodies of ordinary cultivators. This means that instead of manipulating the leaders of the planet, they’ve marked open forsaken gates for them; she can merely help her people come through a special ritual.
Aside from that, a forsaken seer can also predict and weave complex plans into motion. Basically, they are dangerous adversaries to contend with.
Everything is within their calculation.
"300 years ago, she came to this planet with a deal. We were to provide her with cultivators from other planets since most come here to train, and in return, she would help us leave this place."
Lilixen stopped there, knowing that what she had to say next would, without a doubt, anger Kent. So she ignored that and said the next best thing.
"She predicted you would come after taking the four Foxkins away and branding the other with a curse before sending her away half dead."
"Did she mention me by name?"
"No," Azrakul answered, his body shivering from the coldness. "However, she said someone would come, and when they do, we should stop them at all costs."
"I see." Kent looked deeply at the three Monarchs... "How can I get to her?"
Khar’mul pointed at a mountain in the distance... "She mostly comes from that place with her people."
"And how many are they, and their strength?"
"We don’t know her strength level, but the others are at the Death Stage. The last time they came for the four foxes, there were 20 of them."
"That wasn’t too hard now, was it?" Kent smiled and unfurled his wings, slowly rising to the sky.
"You can melt the ice on your own as a punishment for obstructing my business," Kent said coldly before flapping his wings. In no time, he was shooting toward the mountain.
The three Monarchs were left shivering as if they had vibrators in their bodies. They had themselves to blame for coming against a monster like Kent.
Many died because they chose to defy him.
Now, although he left them alive, it will take them a couple of months to fully clear the ice. But even so, the coldness will linger for a while.
Kent didn’t even use the absolute coldness of his ice this time. However, even so, the coldness left behind wouldn’t be easy to handle.
It would take them time and energy to do that.

Maybe this was his way of telling the three Monarchs to behave next time. Kent knew that if he killed the three of them, the planet would become chaotic, preventing future cultivators from having a good time to train.

However, with the three Monarchs around, the planet will hold an order and some semblance of quiet. Of course, in the end, it is a lawless world, with every cultivator having the obligation to kill every living being on it.
That was how it was designed, and as such, Kent wouldn’t have been punished if he wiped every living soul on it.

But even though he didn’t, he had farmed some tower points and, most importantly, blood essence. Although not enough on both fronts, being able to clear some of his debt and inch closer to reaching Level 4 Spirit Lord is also good.
Kent landed on the mountain with a mighty tremble.
He had already located the teleportation gate, so right when he landed, the tower quickly started activating it.
[Master, should I summon Uncle Drew and the others? From what the Monarch Beasts said, there is a chance you will be walking into a trap.]
Kent smiled, sensing the worry in the tower’s words.

Although there is a need to worry, considering the Forsaken race isn’t restricted by planetary limitations, Kent knows too much to understand better. He knew that in the high world, the chances of many Immortals being among the forsaken race were very low.
This is because it takes a lot to take a cultivator from the Death Stage to the Root Immortal Stage. The treasures involved can’t easily be found in high worlds.
But even if they have the necessary treasures, the energy in the high worlds isn’t enough to aid ascension from the Death Stage to the Root Immortal Stage.
Basically, it will take a lot for that to happen. So, on a planet full of Forsaken beings in a high world, there might be fewer than a dozen Immortals.
Of course, Kent isn’t underestimating them. He is too intelligent to make such a mistake. However, while he isn’t underestimating them, he also isn’t looking down on himself.
The last thing he would do is be afraid of a Forsaken being. Even if what is waiting for him on the other side is a god, Kent isn’t going to cower.
He hates the Forsaken race just too much to fear them.
[This is a trap for sure.]
’Oh, trust me, I know. From what I know of their summoning ritual, the stronger the person’s innate talent, the stronger the Forsaken being that can be summoned into their bodies.
And knowing the history of the Forsaken Seers, she had probably used the three Monarchs as a test to see if someone extraordinary would appear.’
[All the more reason the master should call for backup.]
’Where is the fun in that?’ Kent grinned, watching as the gate opened. ’After the battle in the Paragon Universe, I haven’t had that much fun yet. I have become even more powerful now.
So why don’t I use this moment to test out a few things? I mean, wouldn’t you like to see what the Primordial Chaos Dragon is capable of?’
[I suppose the master does have a point. In any case, if the master ended up biting more than he can chew, I will act to save his life.]
’Suit yourself... Though I doubt there will be a need for that.’
Kent took a step forward, and soon, he walked into the teleportation gate.

chapters.title: Chapter 1250: Atarah
paragraphs: It takes one with both confidence and absolute strength, and some form of craziness, to willingly walk into a trap, knowing the outcome can’t be determined based on assumption.
A preplanned trap always has layers of reinforcement to ensure it captures the one they want.
Walking into the teleportation gate, Kent knew there was danger waiting for him on the other side.
However, inasmuch as he would like to turn and leave, learning that the one involved is a forsaken seer, his anger had clouded his judgment.
The endgame is always to uproot the forsaken race from the face of the universe.
To many, the forsaken race had been sealed away. However, to Kent, he knew one day, they would come, and many would die as before.
So to prevent that, he wouldn’t let any opportunity to kill, even if a dozen of them passed him by. He is too committed to let such a chance slip away.
Hatred and heartbreak have a way of making even the best of society extremely bitter.
In the end, Kent walked through the teleportation gate only to appear at the centre of a killing formation created by thousands of dragons.
"Hmmm"
Kent made a low hum, slowly lifting his eye to see what danger he had stepped into.
His gaze met that of a pale-looking lady with white horns and a thin ring of Immortal Qi moving around her. She has a slender physique, with little to see on her chest and back.
However, the look in her eyes – piercing and scrutinising – told Kent that he had indeed stepped into a wild one.
’A Root Immortal,’ Kent made no facial expression. However, deep down, his heart was beating wildly. ’Oh, this is going to be fun.’
[How is this going to be fun, master? From what I see, we have a peak Root Immortal, who is a forsaken being. 4 high-level Root Immortals, also forsaken beings.
200 Death stage, 1200 Life stage, 20,000 Empyreans, and over 400,000 Heavenly Ascension stage cultivators with nothing but murder in their eyes.
I may not be a person, but there is no way this is going to be fun at all.]
Kent smiled and shook his head, ’Maybe to them. However, from where I stand, I see billions of Tower Points, Blood Essence, and Soul Spirits begging me to harvest them.
If that is not going to be fun, then I don’t know what would.’
[You are crazy.]
’No, I am not. My mom had me tested.’
Kent chuckled.
There are only 24 forsaken beings. Five of them are Immortals, and the rest are dragons with forsaken blood in them.
This allowed them to bypass the limit of high worlds, allowing most of them to reach the Death stage. Kent had already encountered someone before with a similar arrangement.
However, unlike him, who failed to complete the merger of the two bloodlines, the dragons seem to have achieved that, lifting the planet restriction off the cultivation.
However, Kent knew, deep down, that things aren’t as simple as they appear. Even so, he let the moment become funny to him.
He didn’t expect dragons to go into bed with the forsaken race... not when their ancestor, the Chaos Dragon, had killed billions of them.

"Are you having your last smile before a Forsaken King takes over your body?" Suddenly, the pale-looking lady whom Kent knew to be the forsaken seer spoke, a wave of Immortal Qi mixed with forsaken qi pouring from her body.
Kent stopped smiling and focused his attention on her. "And you are—"
The pale lady turned ashen, her expression switching between anger and embarrassment.
"Insolent." Suddenly, a death stage forsaken being lunged at Kent, a spear aimed for his chest, waves of forsaken qi emitting from it.
"Tch," Kent chuckled and raised his right index finger. Waves of ice condensed at the tip, causing the space around him to turn cold. Then, with a sudden command, he shot a thin beam of ice.
"Begone."

The ice beam moved faster than the wind and drew a thin hole through his forehead. No blood came out, just the sudden and instant snuffing of life that the forsaken man used to hold dear to his chest.
His body stopped midair and fell, slamming to the ground with a loud thud.
’Although I hate you bastards, you sure have potent blood essence.’ Kent chuckled, feeling the potent energy wash into his [Blood Core.]

He raised his head and looked at the forsaken seer. "Well, care to tell me who you are and why you placed a curse on the mother of my little friend? Also, while you’re at it, care to tell me where the four you took are?"
The ashen expression on her face turned cold. Then she lifted her staff and, with a cold tone, spoke... "I, Atarah, would make sure that before your body is taken away, you would suffer."
"Looks like we share the same thought. However, while killing you all 24 will give me pleasure, the rest of you... as a fellow dragon, I am very disappointed in you.
Where is your pride as a dragon? Bending over to let the forsaken race fuck you is the last thing I ever expected from you lot."
The thousands of dragons roared, releasing powerful dragon authority, all aimed at Kent.
"Oh, please, stop tickling me."
Kent extended his hands, and they turned into razor-sharp claws ending in piercing talons.
"KILL HIM BUT KEEP HIS BODY INTACT!" Atarah commanded, and Kent felt the weight of attacks come from all directions.
The first barrage of attacks slammed toward him like a collapsing star. He, a lone dragon, stood under a devastating barrage of attacks, all coming from beings that could flatten any High World.
’Tower, say roughly, how much in Tower Points would I be earning after this slaughter?’ Instead of fear, Kent chose to calculate his gains.
He is facing five Immortals and hundreds of Death-stage cultivators, after all, not to mention the thousands of others.
[The master can rest assured that he will be paying off his debt if he lives to tell the tale.]
’Ah, lucky me.’
Waves of deadly dragon breath, Immortal Qi blasts, and chaotic flames blasted toward him, tearing the air like it was made of paper.
The world trembled for miles, space vibrating violently under the crushing force directed at him.
Kent didn’t move.
Instead, he simply narrowed his eyes at the approaching danger... and the temperature around him plummeted.
A dome of pale-blue frost erupted from beneath his feet, expanding outward like a blooming flower. It expanded large enough before coming to a halt.
Every attack that entered the frost domain slowed, thickened, and then froze mid-flight.
Dragon flames turned to ice sculptures, Immortal Qi beams shattered like they were mere brittle glass, and physical strikes stopped completely as though the world itself paused.
"I love ice." Kent grinned.
With a flick of his wrist, the frozen barrage exploded into powdery dust.
ROAR
A chaotic roar escaped his mouth, causing the hundreds of thousands of dragons to feel their bodies tense.
"Let the killing begin." Kent locked his eyes on two of the Root Immortals.
His claws glimmered coldly, then, tapping into the soul map’s scanning range, he vanished and reappeared behind one of them.

sentences.text: It takes one with both confidence and absolute strength, and some form of craziness, to willingly walk into a trap, knowing the outcome can’t be determined based on assumption.
A preplanned trap always has layers of reinforcement to ensure it captures the one they want.
Walking into the teleportation gate, Kent knew there was danger waiting for him on the other side.
However, inasmuch as he would like to turn and leave, learning that the one involved is a forsaken seer, his anger had clouded his judgment.
The endgame is always to uproot the forsaken race from the face of the universe.
To many, the forsaken race had been sealed away.
However, to Kent, he knew one day, they would come, and many would die as before.
So to prevent that, he wouldn’t let any opportunity to kill, even if a dozen of them passed him by.
He is too committed to let such a chance slip away.
Hatred and heartbreak have a way of making even the best of society extremely bitter.
In the end, Kent walked through the teleportation gate only to appear at the centre of a killing formation created by thousands of dragons.
"Hmmm"
Kent made a low hum, slowly lifting his eye to see what danger he had stepped into.
His gaze met that of a pale-looking lady with white horns and a thin ring of Immortal Qi moving around her.
She has a slender physique, with little to see on her chest and back.
However, the look in her eyes – piercing and scrutinising – told Kent that he had indeed stepped into a wild one.
’A Root Immortal,’ Kent made no facial expression.
However, deep down, his heart was beating wildly. ’Oh, this is going to be fun.’
[How is this going to be fun, master?
From what I see, we have a peak Root Immortal, who is a forsaken being.
4 high-level Root Immortals, also forsaken beings.
200 Death stage, 1200 Life stage, 20,000 Empyreans, and over 400,000 Heavenly Ascension stage cultivators with nothing but murder in their eyes.
I may not be a person, but there is no way this is going to be fun at all.]
Kent smiled and shook his head, ’Maybe to them.
However, from where I stand, I see billions of Tower Points, Blood Essence, and Soul Spirits begging me to harvest them.
If that is not going to be fun, then I don’t know what would.’
[You are crazy.]
’No, I am not.
My mom had me tested.’
Kent chuckled.
There are only 24 forsaken beings.
Five of them are Immortals, and the rest are dragons with forsaken blood in them.
This allowed them to bypass the limit of high worlds, allowing most of them to reach the Death stage.
Kent had already encountered someone before with a similar arrangement.
However, unlike him, who failed to complete the merger of the two bloodlines, the dragons seem to have achieved that, lifting the planet restriction off the cultivation.
However, Kent knew, deep down, that things aren’t as simple as they appear.
Even so, he let the moment become funny to him.
He didn’t expect dragons to go into bed with the forsaken race... not when their ancestor, the Chaos Dragon, had killed billions of them.

"Are you having your last smile before a Forsaken King takes over your body?" Suddenly, the pale-looking lady whom Kent knew to be the forsaken seer spoke, a wave of Immortal Qi mixed with forsaken qi pouring from her body.
Kent stopped smiling and focused his attention on her.
"And you are—"
The pale lady turned ashen, her expression switching between anger and embarrassment.
"Insolent." Suddenly, a death stage forsaken being lunged at Kent, a spear aimed for his chest, waves of forsaken qi emitting from it.
"Tch," Kent chuckled and raised his right index finger.
Waves of ice condensed at the tip, causing the space around him to turn cold.
Then, with a sudden command, he shot a thin beam of ice.
"Begone."
The ice beam moved faster than the wind and drew a thin hole through his forehead.
No blood came out, just the sudden and instant snuffing of life that the forsaken man used to hold dear to his chest.
His body stopped midair and fell, slamming to the ground with a loud thud.
’Although I hate you bastards, you sure have potent blood essence.’ Kent chuckled, feeling the potent energy wash into his [Blood Core.]
He raised his head and looked at the forsaken seer.
"Well, care to tell me who you are and why you placed a curse on the mother of my little friend?
Also, while you’re at it, care to tell me where the four you took are?"
The ashen expression on her face turned cold.
Then she lifted her staff and, with a cold tone, spoke...
"I, Atarah, would make sure that before your body is taken away, you would suffer."
"Looks like we share the same thought.
However, while killing you all 24 will give me pleasure, the rest of you... as a fellow dragon, I am very disappointed in you.
Where is your pride as a dragon?
Bending over to let the forsaken race fuck you is the last thing I ever expected from you lot."
The thousands of dragons roared, releasing powerful dragon authority, all aimed at Kent.
"Oh, please, stop tickling me."
Kent extended his hands, and they turned into razor-sharp claws ending in piercing talons.
"KILL HIM BUT KEEP HIS BODY INTACT!" Atarah commanded, and Kent felt the weight of attacks come from all directions.
The first barrage of attacks slammed toward him like a collapsing star.
He, a lone dragon, stood under a devastating barrage of attacks, all coming from beings that could flatten any High World.
’Tower, say roughly, how much in Tower Points would I be earning after this slaughter?’ Instead of fear, Kent chose to calculate his gains.
He is facing five Immortals and hundreds of Death-stage cultivators, after all, not to mention the thousands of others.
[The master can rest assured that he will be paying off his debt if he lives to tell the tale.]
’Ah, lucky me.’
Waves of deadly dragon breath, Immortal Qi blasts, and chaotic flames blasted toward him, tearing the air like it was made of paper.
The world trembled for miles, space vibrating violently under the crushing force directed at him.
Kent didn’t move.
